observations: Photo 0: DSLR camera body with 'Canon' and 'EOS 650D' text visible on body, mounted with a Canon zoom lens, lens cap on.
Photo 0: Lens barrel shows 'Canon' branding and focal markings partially visible (18-55 range implied by cap on front).
Photo 1: Rear of camera showing flip-out LCD screen (screen appears closed/dark, not powered on), viewfinder, MENU/INFO buttons, control dial.

Photo 2: Top view showing lens zoom ring with markings '18-24-35-55mm', mode dial (M, Av, Tv, P, Auto, Video), ON/OFF switch, hot shoe, and what appears to be an open memory card door on the side with no card visible.
No photo shows the camera powered on, a sample image, a shutter count screen, or the lens glass/elements for fungus or scratch inspection.
No battery, charger, or box shown in any photo.
Watermark 'MCSTEVE POSTED ON JIJI' overlaid on all images, consistent with marketplace listing rather than a fraud indicator by itself.

claims.evidence: Cosmetic condition looks reasonable in photos 0-2 but lens glass and sensor are not shown, and 'sharp' (image quality) cannot be judged from product photos alone.
No import sticker, UK retailer tag, or serial/warranty card shown in any photo to confirm origin.
No photo shows the camera powered on, a shutter actuation count, a live view/LCD display active, or a test shot. The screen in photo 1 appears off.

risks.risk: Shutter count unknown — a heavily used shutter affects long-term value even if currently working.
risks.proof: Photo or screenshot of shutter count from camera menu or third-party shutter-count software/tool.
risks.if_unproven: priced as high/unknown shutter count (lower end of working-camera range)

risks.risk: Sensor condition (dust, scratches, dead pixels) not visible in listing photos.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of sensor with mirror up, or a test photo taken against plain white/blue sky showing no spots.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not confirmed clean, assume possible sensor dust

risks.risk: LCD screen functionality — screen is shown closed and not illuminated in any photo.
risks.proof: Photo or clip of camera powered on with LCD displaying menu or live view.
risks.if_unproven: priced as screen not confirmed working

risks.risk: Lens optical condition (fungus, haze, scratches on glass elements) not shown.
risks.proof: Photo of front and rear lens elements under light, showing clear glass with no fungus/haze.
risks.if_unproven: priced as lens condition unconfirmed, assume possible fungus/haze

risks.risk: No battery, charger, or memory card shown — accessory completeness unverified, affects total value/usability.
risks.proof: Photo showing battery, charger, and memory card included with the camera.
risks.if_unproven: priced as body+lens only, accessories not included

risks.risk: Autofocus and image stabilization (lens has 'STABILIZER' switch per photo 2) function not demonstrated.
risks.proof: Short video clip showing autofocus locking and lens stabilizer engaging.
risks.if_unproven: priced as AF/IS unconfirmed, treat as potentially faulty

risks.risk: Overall camera power-on and basic operation (shutter fire, image capture) not demonstrated.
risks.proof: Video clip of camera powering on, taking a photo, and reviewing it on screen.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not working (worst case per rules)

proof_requests: Video of the camera powering on, focusing, and firing the shutter with image review on LCD.
Photo of shutter count from camera info menu or EXIF data from a test shot.
Close-up photos of front and rear lens elements under bright light.
Photo of included accessories (battery, charger, memory card, box) if any.
Photo of a test image taken with the camera to assess image quality and sensor cleanliness.
response.reason: The item is clearly identified as a Canon EOS 650D body with an EF-S 18-55mm kit lens from readable text in the photos, but no photo or clip demonstrates the camera is powered on or functional, so per the rules this is priced at worst case as not working until proof is provided.
